title: The categorical palette's first two slots are too close for full colour vision
foundBy: independent review of the palette work, which found the decision CUI-084 recorded as needed and then closed without making

evidence.verified:
`npm run ci` exits 0. The palette gate reports 16 contracts holding where it reported 14, the two new ones being the categorical normal-vision check in each theme: 15.4 dark at #ce747a<->#a29cda and 15.4 light at #3b5e8c<->#358f84, against a floor of 15.

The new check was proved to fail rather than assumed to. Putting the old #6f93c9 and #4fb3a6 back made the gate report `--color-cat-* dark normal 12.2`, which is the figure this record was filed on, and the file was restored afterwards. A unit test in `scripts/check-palette.test.mjs` pins the same case against the whole six-slot set this package shipped before, so the failure is held at both levels.

What the change did to the rest of the contract, measured rather than assumed. The worst colour-blind separation improved from 9.4 to 11.0 dark and from 8.0 to 10.0 light. The worst contrast against the binding surface moved from 5.79 to 5.20 dark and from 3.56 to 3.46 light, both still over the 3.0 a graphical object needs. Mean chroma rose 1.2 per cent dark and 1.5 per cent light, which is the whole price paid in mutedness. At seven slots the palette still fails, at 6.3 dark and 4.4 light, so the six-slot cap still stands.

The visual change was audited rather than eyeballed. Twelve of 112 captures moved, all of them chart, dashboard or event-lane pages, in both themes symmetrically, and the other 100 are byte-identical. Every one of the 644,275 changed pixels was checked against the identity that a same-slot change makes the pixel delta a non-negative combination of slot deltas, with the surface cancelling out: 100.000 per cent of them fit, so no pixel changed for any reason but a categorical slot moving. `visual-baseline/render-image.json` shows the same two image digests as the committed baseline, so the captures are comparable and the renderer did not move. Axe reports 0 violations in both themes and 0 rules matching more nodes than the baseline. Both themes were also looked at: the five bars of the chart pattern separate cleanly and the set still reads as muted.

details:
`--color-cat-1` and `--color-cat-2` separate by 12.2 against a floor of 15, for a reader whose vision is not simulated at all. They are the first two slots, so they are the two series of any two-series chart drawn with this palette, and `--color-cat-5` against `--color-cat-6` measures 9.9.

This is not the colour-blind collapse CUI-084 was about. It is a separate miss, in the common case rather than a specialised one, and a reader with full colour vision meets it.

CUI-084's own note of 2026-09-13 named it and said it needed a decision either way. That record then closed having fixed the eight-slot ramp and capped the categorical contract at six slots, neither of which moves these values. The miss survived the work that was supposed to settle it.

The palette is muted by decision, and mutedness is what puts these hues close together, so this is a trade rather than an oversight to correct blindly. Raising the separation costs some of the muted character that a colour review chose. That is the decision to make.

`scripts/check-palette.mjs` does not hold the categorical palette to the normal-vision floor, and its comment says why and points here. Adding that check without moving the values would fail the build.

notes.text: The gate names this record in a comment, so the exemption is visible in the file rather than inferred from what is absent. That matters because the graph ramp shipped with a contrast failure exactly through a gate that checked less than it appeared to.

Decided by the owner: fix the values rather than document the miss. Two default chart colours that a reader with full colour vision struggles to tell apart is a worse thing for this package to carry than a palette slightly less muted than the one a colour review chose.

So the work is to raise the separation of `--color-cat-1` against `--color-cat-2`, and of any other pair that falls under the floor, while giving up as little of the muted character as the measurements allow. Whoever does it should add the normal-vision check to the categorical contract in `scripts/check-palette.mjs` at the same time, and remove the exemption its comment records, so the gate holds the palette to what it now claims.

This changes what existing consumers see, so it re-records visual captures and belongs in the changelog as a breaking change alongside the six-slot narrowing.

Two corrections to this record, found while fixing it.

It says `--color-cat-5` against `--color-cat-6` measures 9.9. Those two measure 18.0 dark and 19.7 light. The pair that measures 9.9 is `--color-cat-5` against `--color-cat-9`, which is neither adjacent nor inside the six slots the contract covers, so it is not a pair this contract governs at all.

It also understates the problem by naming one failing pair. Five adjacent pairs sat under the floor: 1-2 at 12.2, 3-4 at 13.8 and 4-5 at 12.4 in the dark theme, and 1-2 at 12.6 and 3-4 at 12.1 in the light one. The owner's ruling already covered them, because it said to raise any pair under the floor rather than only the first two.

How the values were chosen, since the ruling asked for as little mutedness given up as the measurements allow. The six slots were searched in OKLCH by annealing, with chroma increases penalised about three times as hard as decreases, hue shifts penalised lightly and lightness treated as the cheap axis, subject to every floor the contract states plus a margin.

Lightness and hue turned out to carry almost all of it. Mean chroma rose 1.2 per cent dark and 1.5 per cent light, no slot moved more than 0.034 in lightness or 8.6 degrees in hue, and light `--color-cat-6` did not move at all. The hue names in the stylesheet and in section 4.12 still describe the colours.

Contrast was held as a floor of 3.45 rather than the contract's 3.0, because an early search traded light `--color-cat-3` down from 3.56 to 3.17 to buy separation. Nothing in the contract forbids that, and it spends a margin this package had rather than one it was given.
